1.title: Azure Compute
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Azure Compute. It covers the exam area Describe Azure architecture and services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Compare compute types, including containers, virtual machines, and functions. Describe virtual machine options, including Azure virtual machines, Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets, availability sets, and Azure Virtual Desktop. Describe the resources required for virtual machines. Describe application hosting options, including web apps, containers, and virtual machines. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Describe Azure architecture and services (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A Z nine hundred study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Compute types compared
1.text: Compute types compared. Virtual machines. What it is: Emulated computers that run an operating system. You manage: O S, patches, software, scaling. Best for: Full control, lift and shift, custom software. Containers. What it is: Lightweight packages of an app with what it needs, sharing the host O S. You manage: The app image (and orchestration if used). Best for: Microservices, fast start, portable apps.

1.title: Compute types compared, continued
1.text: Compute types compared. Functions (serverless). What it is: Small pieces of code that run on events. You manage: Only the code. Best for: Event-driven tasks, automation, pay per run. Exam tip: More control equals more to manage. V Ms are the most control, functions the least. A container is lighter than a V M because it does not include a full operating system.

1.title: Compute types compared, continued
1.text: Compute types compared. The figure shows this: Virtual machines, containers and functions compared by how much you manage.

1.title: Virtual machines (Azure Virtual Machines)
1.text: Virtual machines (Azure Virtual Machines). Azure Virtual Machines give you a server you control. You choose the size, operating system (Windows or Linux) and software. Use V Ms when you need total control of the O S, run custom or legacy software, or do a lift and shift. You are responsible for patching and maintenance of the guest O S.

1.title: VM options
1.text: V M options. Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Create and manage a group of identical, load-balanced V Ms; the number of instances can grow or shrink automatically with demand or a schedule. Availability sets. Spread V Ms across fault domains (separate hardware, power, network) and update domains (groups rebooted together during maintenance) inside one datacenter, so one failure or update does not take all V Ms down.

1.title: VM options, continued
1.text: V M options. Availability zones (Module four). Place V Ms in separate datacenters of a region for stronger protection. Azure Virtual Desktop. A desktop and app virtualization service in the cloud: users reach a Windows desktop from nearly any device. Exam tip: Scale set equals identical V Ms, autoscale. Availability set equals protect from hardware failure and planned maintenance within a datacenter. Azure Virtual Desktop equals remote desktops delivered from Azure. Zones are better than sets for datacenter-level failure.

1.title: Resources a VM needs
1.text: Resources a V M needs. A V M is not just the machine. Creating one usually involves. Compute (the V M itself: size, C P U, memory). Runs the O S and apps. Storage (O S disk, optional data disks). Holds the operating system and data. Networking (virtual network, subnet, network interface). Connects the V M. Public I P address (optional). Reach the V M from the internet. Network security group (optional but common). Filters traffic with rules.

1.title: Containers
1.text: Containers. A container packages an application and its dependencies and shares the host operating system, so it starts faster and uses fewer resources than a V M. Azure Container Instances (A C I). Run a container quickly without managing V Ms or an orchestrator; good for simple apps and short jobs. Azure Kubernetes Service (A K S). A managed Kubernetes service to deploy, scale and manage many containers (orchestration). Azure Container Apps. Serverless containers for microservices without managing Kubernetes. Exam tip: One or a few containers, no orchestration to A C I. Many containers, orchestration, scaling to A K S.

1.title: Azure Functions
1.text: Azure Functions. Azure Functions is serverless: you write code that runs when an event (trigger) happens, such as an H T T P request, a timer or a new file. Azure scales it automatically and, on the consumption model, you pay only while it runs. Use it for small, event-driven tasks, such as processing an uploaded file or running a job on a schedule.

1.title: Application hosting options
1.text: Application hosting options. Azure App Service (web apps). Type: pass. Use it when: You build web apps, A P Is and mobile back ends and do not want to manage servers. It supports several languages and gives built-in scaling and deployment. Containers (A C I, A K S). Type: Containers. Use it when: The app is packaged as containers or built as microservices.

1.title: Application hosting options, continued
1.text: Application hosting options. Virtual machines. Type: I A A S. Use it when: You need full O S control or must run custom software. Azure Functions. Type: Serverless. Use it when: The code is event driven and short. Choose: web app, no server work to App Service; packaged app to containers; special software or legacy server to V M; event-triggered snippets to Functions.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants a group of identical web servers that adds instances automatically when traffic rises. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Scale sets manage identical, load-balanced V Ms and can autoscale. An availability set only spreads V Ms across fault and update domains.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team wants to run a single container quickly without managing servers or an orchestrator. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Azure Container Instances. A C I runs containers without V M or orchestrator management. A K S is for orchestrating many containers.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A developer wants to host a web app without managing the operating system. Which option fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Azure App Service. App Service is a pass offering for web apps and A P Is.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which resources does a typical Azure virtual machine need in addition to compute? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Storage and networking. A V M needs storage for its disks and networking (virtual network and interface), with optional public I P and network security group.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Employees need to use a Windows desktop hosted in Azure from any device. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Azure Virtual Desktop. Azure Virtual Desktop delivers desktops and apps from the cloud.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Code must run only when a new file arrives, and the company wants to pay only while it runs. Which compute type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Functions. Functions are event-driven serverless code billed for execution.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which compute type gives the most control? Answer: Virtual machines. Question two. Why is a container lighter than a V M? Answer: It shares the host operating system instead of including a full one. Question three. What is the difference between a scale set and an availability set? Answer: A scale set manages identical V Ms that autoscale; an availability set spreads V Ms over fault and update domains in one datacenter.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which service orchestrates many containers? Answer: Azure Kubernetes Service (A K S). Question five. What starts an Azure function? Answer: A trigger (event), such as H T T P, a timer or a new file. Question six. Which hosting option is pass for web apps? Answer: Azure App Service.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. V Ms: I A A S; full control; you patch the O S; lift and shift. Scale Sets: identical V Ms, load balanced, autoscale. Availability set: fault and update domains in one datacenter; zones are stronger. Azure Virtual Desktop: cloud desktops and apps for users. V M resources: compute, storage (disks), networking, optional public I P and N S G. Containers: share host O S; A C I equals quick and simple; A K S equals orchestration. Functions: serverless, event triggers, pay per execution. App Service: pass for web apps and A P Is. In the next module, we continue the course.
